title: Reduce complete sparse recurrence CLI time by 45.68% (no κ)
body:
## Summary

Two lines skip exact-zero row updates in the complete coupled-recurrence certificate producer. The full 64-type half-chain CLI median falls from **67.50 ms to 36.67 ms**, a **45.68% reduction**, across five alternating fresh-process pairs. Every complete certificate is byte-identical. This is a scoped implementation-equivalence result with finite conformance and local performance evidence, **no new κ**.

```diff
 for i in range(k+1,n):
+    if rows[i][k] == 0:
+        continue
     factor = rows[i][k]/rows[k][k]
```

At an exact zero coefficient and the existing positive pivot, the old factor is zero and every skipped assignment leaves the same rational value. Both certificate alternatives, forcing solve, verifier, serialization budget, input validation and CLI stay intact. [Proof and bounds](research/sparse-coupled-certificate/PROOF.md) and [reproduction](research/sparse-coupled-certificate/README.md) are in the opt-in package.

The new implementation, conformance bridge and measurements were produced by Nick Petalas. Credit Ali Romman / #5785 for the complete producer/checker and retained recurrence lineage. Zero-elimination skipping is classical; thakrarsagar / #736 previously applied it to a different cyclotomic-inverse replay. Neither mathematical predecessor is being re-audited here.

## Evidence

- Before: a complete untimed cProfile run records 107,776 Fraction multiplications and 95,616 subtractions, dominated by exact arithmetic in elimination. The first accepted mechanism removes zero-coefficient work.
- After: all ten complete benchmark CLIs succeed, with zero errors, zero stdout mismatches and the same input-hash-bound certificate bytes. Baseline range 66.94–68.99 ms; changed range 36.42–36.91 ms. Same interpreter, flags, input and helper bytes; every sample is retained below. The workload is the existing maximum-size test's 64-type half-chain with forcing one.
- Exact old/current conformance passes **286 fixture executions**, comprising 50 contracting and 236 noncontracting results. Full certificates agree, both verifiers accept both producers, and input values are preserved. Coverage includes the complete two-type coefficient grid, sparse/dense sizes through 64, early/late noncontraction, coupling-driven failure and a near-boundary case.
- Six malformed inputs, three false certificates and two source-byte mutations reject. The existing six repository tests pass, including the portable CLI and serialization boundary. Actual corruption of each of the two exported live source files also rejects under optimized Python.
- Warning-strict direct normal and optimized commands pass in 0.444 s and 0.420 s; their complete generated receipts agree. Registered replay passes in 1.133 s. Each registered check has a 60-second cap. AST compilation, function-size inspection and staged whitespace checks pass.
- Exact committed bytes, modes and source ancestry pass at `d2d528a7220b79d9ef150c57237e0ee07c912f5e`. Official export integrity and both declared inputs pass. Normal and optimized replays in a read-only Git-free export with empty PATH agree with the checkout; all eleven exported files retain their bytes and modes. Existing benchmark output files reject without modification.

From the repository root, CPython 3.12 and the standard library:

```sh

```

Use a corresponding Python 3.12 path elsewhere and a fresh external benchmark output path. Scientific markers are `PASS_SPARSE_COUPLED_CERTIFICATE` and `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`. The benchmark reconstructs the exact baseline by removing only the guard, authenticates both versions and the helper, and times complete fresh CLI processes. It does not time the conformance loader or omit internal verification.

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The measured improvement is for this one local sparse CLI workload on macOS arm64, with five samples per side. No dense, universal-input, cross-platform or full-frontier speedup is claimed. The equivalence argument covers the original bounded accepted interface; finite conformance alone is not a formal proof.

The benchmark uses POSIX load reporting and is optional. Scientific conformance has no timing threshold. Dynamic exact arithmetic and the bounded authenticated comparison seam are documented in PROOF.md. No selected scientific cold replay, native/caller/compiler admission, Lean, Docker or full multiplication theorem was run. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Selected κ .003125804 and all five framework assumptions remain.

## Open next questions

Does an actual coupled caller still spend most time in elimination after this guard? Profile its complete matrix and forcing before choosing another optimization. No further consumer or construction is reserved.

## Related open work

Completion refresh inspected the fifteen other account PRs still open and created since the advance CLAIM. None modifies `scripts/certify_coupled_recurrence.py` or reports timing for the same 64-type CLI workload. No same-instance numerical disagreement was identified, and no extra predecessor computations were run.

- #6271 proves minimum paid switching periods for synchronized two-type recursive modes. Its switched recurrence contract is separate from this fixed-matrix certificate implementation; no common runtime or numerical result is compared.
- #3898 binds a selected stage-one stock recurrence. It supplies a source-coverage obligation and does not modify this certificate implementation; no common numerical claim is compared.

Canonical main was refreshed unchanged at `2485805a6d47f36ea83ddde6327d453ac82d44dc`, priority revision 8, before committing. The selected binding-only orientation passes. Main-tree and merged/all-state searches include the general coupled-tool and zero-elimination terms. Coverage is bounded; unpublished work and arbitrary historical diffs are not covered. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19294807).

## CI notes

Both hosted checks, `plan` and `replay (research/sparse-coupled-certificate)`, passed at head `d2d528a7220b79d9ef150c57237e0ee07c912f5e` in [run 41069209556](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41069209556). The completed check list was read once; the run metadata confirms the matching head, completed status and successful conclusion.

All local checks above also passed. Hosted replay passes the registered normal/optimized finite conformance checks; the local timing percentage is not a CI benchmark assertion. Supplier admission and independent human/formal proof-kernel review remain unclaimed. No CI failure remains to report.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way. The production change is the two-line zero guard.

**Blast Radius:** certificate tool. One shared script and eight new evidence-package files change. The existing contributor notice, frozen packages, upstream archives and selected record are untouched.
